MAP LAYERS

Topography shows contours every 50 m, with brighter lines every 250 m, interpolated between elevation cells. Hazards shade slopes steeper than 10°, 18° and 22°, the three route limits. Other layers come from the loaded files and are reprojected onto the reference grid; they are shown for reference only and are not used in route calculations. Lower the overlay opacity to check how a layer lines up with the elevation map.

Terrain slopes are calculated between elevation samples. Rocks and other hazards below the raster resolution are outside the model. Elevation source for Jezero: USGS Mars 2020 CTX DEM.

Data files

Select one or more GeoTIFF files to load together. Files are aligned onto one reference grid using their georeferencing. Only elevation is used to calculate routes; every other layer is shown for reference only.

How to add your own data files
  1. Get a GeoTIFF of Mars (.tif or .tiff) that has map coordinates. Elevation models are available from USGS Astrogeology and the USGS HiRISE and CTX elevation catalogue.
  2. Add it: click Browse computer… (the file is copied into the data/ folder, up to 4 GB), or copy it into data/ yourself and click Refresh list.
  3. Check the Contents column. Each band is identified as elevation, thermal, minerals, geology or imagery. If a band shows as Unidentified, put a <file name>.layers.json file next to it that says what it holds, for example {"bands": {"1": {"kind": "elevation", "units": "m"}}}.
  4. Tick the files to use together. Include at least one elevation file to calculate routes. The alignment preview shows how the files overlap; files from another area or another planet are not loaded, and the reason is shown.
  5. Click Load selected files. The map reloads with a layer button and legend for each file.

Files labelled Included with the repository come with the project. Hide removes a file from this list without deleting it.
